free_tier.stated: Quoted: 'Waifly's free plan gives 300 MB of RAM, 1 GB of storage, one server and one MySQL database for €0 permanently, with CPU capped at 30% and no credit card required.'

per_object_cap.stated: quoted: '1 server, 1 MySQL database' on the free plan. An extra server slot costs EUR 1 a month, which is a paid add-on rather than a free cap.

retention.stated: Quoted: 'A server's status is checked daily; it gets suspended after 3 days offline.' A suspended server created less than 7 days earlier 'is deleted after 3 days'; an older one is kept '15 days' and recoverable from backups.waifly.com. An automated inspection runs every 30 minutes. So the machine persists indefinitely while it keeps running, and dies 3 days after it stops.

egress.terms: not published: no traffic allowance appears on the pricing page, the rules page or the documentation index read today

interface_detail: a Pterodactyl panel with a live console, file manager, SFTP, databases, scheduled tasks and backups; the docs state 'there is no root access or SSH shell'
tooling: the Pterodactyl panel or SFTP; no SSH
chaining: A small always-on application process on a French host: a cron-driven fetch job, a bot, or a tiny API.

limits.value: 300 MB RAM, 1 GB storage, CPU capped at 30 per cent, 1 server
suspended after 3 days offline; deleted 3 days later if younger than 7 days, else 15 days
one account per person, with an automated inspection every 30 minutes

binding_note: 300 MB of RAM with a 30 per cent CPU cap binds first: the anti-abuse rules also forbid tunnels and proxies on the free plan, so the machine cannot be repurposed as a relay when the application outgrows the memory.

identity_cost.detail: no card: quoted 'No payment method is requested for the free plan'. Signup is a username of at least 4 alphanumeric characters, an email, a password of at least 6 characters, a 'how did you find us' field and acceptance of the terms; Discord, Google or Apple login are alternatives. No phone and no document.

reliability_note: The operator publishes 99.9 per cent measured uptime over 30 days on status.waifly.com
confidence_note: Shape, price, the no-card statement and the suspension clock are quoted from the vendor's own documentation read today. Egress is not published, so the row is documented about the allocation and unverified about bandwidth.

quoted: 'A server's status is checked daily; it gets suspended after 3 days offline'; 'Server created less than 7 days ago: deleted after 3 days of suspension'; 'Older server: 15-day retention after suspension'; 'One account per person'; 'VPNs / proxies / tunnels' not allowed on the free plan
quoted: 'No payment method is requested for the free plan'; signup is 'a username of at least 4 alphanumeric characters and a password of at least 6', an email, and acceptance of the terms

quoted: 'Servers are containers managed through a Pterodactyl panel, so there is no root access or SSH shell, but you get a live console, SFTP, databases, scheduled tasks and backups'; 'two Intel Xeon Gold 6138 nodes in Paris'; documentation 'Last updated 2026-08-12'
quoted payment methods: 'PayPal, Stripe (debit/credit card), lava.top ... and cryptocurrencies'. This is what a paid plan accepts; the free plan asks for none

notes: A French host with two named Paris nodes, a documented anti-abuse rule that is unusually explicit about its own suspension clock, and a free plan that needs no card. The founder is named in the documentation (Aubin Devogelaere, 'founder of Waifly') but no company registration number was found on any page read, so the entity is a named individual rather than a company. The one thing that would change the verdict is an egress number, which is not published.

extras.term: permanent while running; suspended 3 days after going offline
extras.price_arithmetic: EUR 0.00 for the free plan; paid plans are EUR 4 (Nano), EUR 8 (Mega) and EUR 16 (Giga) a month, and an extra server slot is EUR 1 a month

network_out.ports: not published for the free plan; paid plans list 2, 5 and 10 ports

session_cap.note: no idle sleep; a server offline for 3 days is suspended, which is a liveness check on the process rather than on traffic

extras.payment_methods: none for the free plan; PayPal, Stripe, lava.top and crypto for paid plans
